transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

Student health sent me here. They said my weight is too low to clear me for the youth workshops, and it’s kept dropping. I mean, I know the number is lower, but it just feels like what happens when I’m busy and focused.
Do you feel overweight?
I don’t know if I’d say overweight exactly, but in photos I go straight to my arms and waist. If I look small enough, I feel like I’m more serious and put-together.
Are you afraid of gaining weight?
Yes. Even gaining a pound makes me panic. If I eat a normal dinner, or something with butter in it, I start thinking everyone will be able to tell I’ve lost discipline.
Do you deliberately limit how much you eat?

Yeah. I plan my day around not really eating—usually just coffee before studio, and maybe a few bites from the café if other people are watching. I avoid bread and anything oily because it feels like it would undo the control I’ve worked for.
Do you ever have episodes where you eat a large amount of food in a short time and feel unable to stop?
I’m not sure what counts as a large amount. I don’t really think I eat that much at once.
Do you ever make yourself vomit after eating?
No, I don’t make myself vomit after I eat.
Do you ever use laxatives, diuretics, or diet pills to keep your weight down?
I’m not really sure what you mean by diet pills. I haven’t noticed using anything like that.
Have your periods stopped?
I’m not sure. I haven’t really been keeping track of that.
Have there been times when you ate what felt like an unusually large amount of food in a short period of time?
I don’t think so. I mean, I eat sometimes, but not an unusually large amount all at once.
When you look in the mirror, do you see yourself as fat?
I guess… in photos from the showcase, I don’t really look at the artwork first. I zoom in on my arms and waist. If I look small enough, I feel more serious and put-together.
Have you used laxatives to try to keep your weight down?
No, I haven’t used laxatives.
After you eat, do you ever make yourself throw up to keep from gaining weight?
I’m not sure what you mean by make myself throw up. I haven’t really noticed doing that.
Have there been times when you felt out of control while eating?
I don’t think so. I usually feel pretty aware of what I’m eating.
Do you exercise specifically to prevent weight gain?
I’m not really sure. What do you mean by exercise specifically for that?
Do you exercise to burn calories or keep from gaining weight?
I mean, I do exercise sometimes, but I’m not sure I’m thinking about it in terms of calories or weight gain.
What is your current height and weight?
I don’t know the exact number offhand. Student health said it was too low to clear me for the youth workshops, and it’s been dropping, but I’ve just been busy and focused.
What is your weight right now?
I don’t know the exact number right now. Student health said it was too low, and that it’s been dropping, but I haven’t really kept track of it.
Have you had times when you felt you ate a lot more food than most people would eat in a similar situation?
I’m not sure what would count as a lot more than most people. I haven’t really noticed having times like that.
Have you been trying to lose weight?

I mean, I plan my day around not eating much. I’ll have coffee before studio, maybe a few bites from the café if people are watching. I avoid bread or anything oily because it feels like it would undo the control I’ve worked for.
Has a doctor told you that your weight is significantly below what is expected for your height?

Student health did say my weight was too low to clear me for the youth workshops. They said it’s kept dropping. I guess I understand that’s why they sent me here, but it just feels like I’ve been focused and busy.
